note: Every number below is read from runs/todomvc-jquery/voyage.json. Sentences are spoken and captioned one at a time.

lines: This is Kane CLI failing an app that an AI agent just rebuilt from scratch.
Step nine failed, and Kane says why.
The test never saved the second counter value, and the screenshots show the app was right.
That report goes straight back to the agent.
The app being rebuilt is this one: TodoMVC in jQuery, from 2012.
Theseus deletes its code, has coding agents grow it back in new stacks, and lets Kane decide when they are done.
Theseus. Delete the code. Keep the ship.
First, capture.
Theseus crawled the running app, and an agent drafted twenty two behaviors in plain English.
Kane ran every one of them on the original app.
Only what Kane proves on the original goes into the spec.
Kane also caught a mistake in our own baseline.
The recorded pass for persist items had added the todos again after reopening the app.
That was a false green.
Theseus verify ran it again, Kane failed it, and the certificate now records it as failed on the original.
Then the code is gone.
Each agent starts in an empty clean room that holds only the spec and reference screenshots, never the original source.
Codex builds a Next.js version and a SvelteKit version side by side.
Kane tests every build in a real browser, with the same plain English sentences it ran on the original.
Next.js round one: twenty of twenty two.
Both failures go back to Codex with the failing step, Kane's reason, its root cause and its suggested fix.
Kane's root causes said the app was right, so Codex left the working code alone.
Kane ran the failures again.
Fresh empty view passed in round two, and the pluralized counter went green in round four.
Twenty two of twenty two.
SvelteKit, also built by Codex in a clean room, passed all twenty two on its first build.
Then a final regression pass ran every behavior on Next.js again.
Kane caught the pluralized counter once more.
Its root cause says the app showed the right counts, and the test did not carry its stored values into the final check.
We count it as a failure anyway. Next.js ends at twenty one of twenty two.
Passing is not the finish line.
Kane stores values while it tests, like the counter text, and Theseus compares them with the values it read on the original.
Next.js: nineteen identical. SvelteKit: twenty identical.
Every divergence and every failure is on the certificate.
All three apps run today. Here are the original and both regrowths, doing the same things.
And here is Kane re-proving one certificate cell on the Next.js build, live, for this video.
A native Android regrowth in Expo is running on the emulator now. Its result is not in yet.
Plain English tests are the only tests that survive a rewrite.
Theseus treats them as the source code.
Built on Kane CLI for the TestMu AI hackathon.
